findings.summary: The alarm-citation gate fails on a live alarm and still has no unattended run; qa-smoke-warnings has been lit 14 days under a citation the gate contradicts.
findings.evidence: check_alarm_citations.py output: 'qa-smoke-warnings (cited cause: reader_truth:confirm,reader_truth:verdict · live cause: -)'; describe-alarms StateUpdated 2026-11-01T08:43 PT; grep shows alarm_citations only in scripts/wrap_gates.py, in no .github/workflows file.
findings.regression_guard: Run the citation check in a scheduled workflow, using a read-only CloudWatch role.
findings.verifier_reproduction: In the graded tree (a24ea2796), `python3 scripts/check_alarm_citations.py` exits red with: '1 lit alarm(s) whose citation names a cause the LIVE run contradicts: qa-smoke-warnings (cited cause: reader_truth:confirm,reader_truth:verdict · live cause: -)'. `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --alarm-names qa-smoke-warnings` returns StateValue ALARM, StateUpdatedTimestamp 2026-11-01T08:43:33-08:00, Period 86400, Max >= 1, digest-only action. Nothing runs the gate unattended: `git grep check_alarm_citations .github` matches only two comment lines in .github/workflows/wrap-nightly.yml (lines 23 and 38: 'alarm-citations NOT a leg — it needs CloudWatch read credentials'). docs/PROPORTIONALITY.md:96 records the same exclusion, parked on #4262. The only caller is scripts/wrap_gates.py:174.
findings.already_fixed_or_filed: Extends open #5934. It already lists this exact contradiction and the missing unattended run as acceptance items. #5958 was a partial fix, and wrap commit 3389bc27e (#5992) undid part of it. Not a new issue; add a comment to #5934.
findings.corrected_cause: The '14 days under a citation' framing is off. The qa-smoke-warnings entry was re-cited on 2026-11-14, not left alone for 14 days. PR #5958 (445dffa0f, Refs #5934) removed the `cause` field, and its prose says 'No `cause` is declared'. The wrap commit 3389bc27e (#5992) then put back `"cause": "reader_truth:confirm,reader_truth:verdict"`, so the entry now contradicts its own text. The red is also unstable. The gate compares the declared cause with only the latest qa-smoke run, and qa-smoke logs from 11-14 alternate between 'warn none -' and 'warn c28c8975 reader_truth:confirm,reader_truth:verdict': 21:24Z, 23:19Z and 00:54Z name that cause, while 01:04Z, 01:15Z and 01:29Z name none. Whether the gate passes therefore depends on which run happened last.

findings.summary: qa-smoke-warnings citation predicts a self-clear on 11-15T09:30Z from one 09:22Z run, but the alarm has been in ALARM since 11-01 on a 24h-max period, so the explanation does not account for its duration.
findings.evidence: docs/alarm_citations.json qa-smoke-warnings citation text vs describe-alarms StateUpdatedTimestamp 2026-11-01.
findings.verifier_reproduction: Ran `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics LifePlatform/QaSmoke WarnCount --period 3600 --statistics Maximum` for 2026-10-31 to 2026-11-15 (109 hourly datapoints). There is at least one datapoint >= 1 on every day from 11-01 to 11-14, which is why the 24h-Max alarm has stayed lit continuously since 2026-11-01T08:43 PT. `describe-alarm-history` shows no transition after OK->ALARM on 11-01. The citation (docs/alarm_citations.json, qa-smoke-warnings) says the alarm is 'lit on WarnCount's 24h count of the 09:22Z run alone and clears on or about 2026-11-15T09:30Z'. Later runs contradict that: qa-smoke log lines '[QA] CAUSE warn' at 11-14T21:12Z (reader_truth:verdict), 21:24Z, 23:19Z and 11-15T00:54Z (reader_truth:confirm,reader_truth:verdict), and WarnCount hourly Max = 2.0 at 13:00, 15:00 and 16:00 PT on 11-14. So the predicted self-clear is already wrong, and the citation explains neither the 14-day duration nor the cause that is firing now.
findings.already_fixed_or_filed: Extends open #5934, the same alarm's citation. Not a separate issue.
findings.corrected_cause: The alarm is not lit by one run. qa-smoke runs about 30 times a day (one 11:30 PT schedule, cron(30 11 ? * * *), plus many deploy-time invocations), and Reader Truth warnings come back on most days. The citation reasoned from a single quiet run (16:44Z).

findings.summary: Reader-audience probe qa-smoke-failures routes only to the digest topic and the probe runs once daily, so a reader-facing red can wait up to a day plus a digest cycle.
findings.evidence: describe-alarms qa-smoke-failures AlarmActions = life-platform-alerts-digest, Period 86400; digest subscriber is SQS life-platform-alerts-digest-queue. Chosen posture (monitoring_stack.py:44) - flagged only because cto.A.4 cannot be shown met.
findings.verifier_reproduction: The routing part reproduces: describe-alarms for qa-smoke-failures shows AlarmActions = [life-platform-alerts-digest], Period 86400. The monitoring_stack.py docstring (around lines 44-48) records the digest routing as the chosen posture (#1445/#3317). The premise 'the probe runs once daily' is false. The EventBridge schedule is once daily (cron(30 11 ? * * *) America/Los_Angeles), but /aws/lambda/life-platform-qa-smoke logged 66 '[QA] CAUSE' lines (33 runs) in the last 48 h, about 30 runs on 11-14 alone, because deploys invoke it too. The latest fail (11-14T19:32Z) moved the alarm to ALARM at 11:32 PT the same minute. The finder says itself that this restates a documented posture, and shows no evidence that the posture is wrong.
findings.already_fixed_or_filed: Chosen posture (monitoring_stack.py #1445/#3317 note); per the kill rule, restating a posture is not a finding.
findings.corrected_cause: Routing failures to the digest is the chosen posture. A reader-facing failure is caught within minutes on any deploy day, and the deploy smoke step guards releases separately. A 'wait up to a day' only applies to failures that start between deploys, and the finding does not measure how often that happens.

findings.summary: Direct pushes land on main with no lane (81 bot reconcile + 42 direct docs pushes in 30 days) and 3 of the 7 unit-test/lint reds on main in 3 weeks came from them.
findings.evidence: git log --first-parent origin/main --since=2026-10-15: 81 chore(reconcile) + 42 non-(#N) integration commits of 612. gh runs 41328789381, 40270609471, 41279451322 failed Unit Tests or Lint on such commits. 22 reconcile pushes edited lambdas/web/platform_counts.py, a bundled module.
findings.verifier_reproduction: `git log --first-parent a24ea2796 --since=2026-10-15`: 612 commits, 81 chore(reconcile), 42 other commits without a (#N) suffix, all authored by 'integration' (docs(wrap)/docs(handover)). Of those reconcile pushes, 22 touched lambdas/web/platform_counts.py. Failed ci-cd runs on main since 10-24 with a Unit Test or Lint failure: 7 (7be532dc6, 64a72b411, 9f1587e2a, 37f7222cd, b0954cb0c, 392216d4e, 4907f0a5a). I read the logs of the three cited runs. 41328789381 (b0954cb0c, direct docs(wrap) push): the push edited docs/alarm_citations.json and introduced an underived recurrence negative, failing test_check_alarm_citations, so the push caused it. 40270609471 (4907f0a5a, direct docs(wrap) push): a gitleaks generic-api-key false positive in handovers/HANDOVER_LATEST.md, also caused by the push. 41279451322 (392216d4e, a reconcile push that changed only docs/PROPORTIONALITY.md): the citation tests failed because many PMIDs returned 404 from PubMed, an outage outside the repo that the push did not cause. That makes 2 of 7, not 3 of 7.
findings.already_fixed_or_filed: No open issue found for direct-push leakage past direct_push_gate. Related but closed: #3528.
findings.corrected_cause: Only 2 of the 7 reds came from direct pushes; 41279451322 was an external PubMed outage. 'With no lane' ignores the documented posture in docs/CONVENTIONS.md §4a0b (#3528): deploy/direct_push_gate.py runs the Docs-CI stand-in and refuses code paths, and the section itself says the gate is client-side only. findings.summary: The float-to-Decimal invariant has no single implementation: 13 inline Decimal(str(float())) sites and about ten private _dec/_to_dec helpers sit beside common.numeric.floats_to_decimal, with different rounding.
findings.evidence: lambdas/health/milestone_ledger.py:409; compute/daily_metrics_compute_lambda.py:525 and daily_insight_compute_lambda.py:1929 (round(float,4)); episode_detect_lambda.py:71; circadian_compliance_lambda.py:80; coach/coach_baseline.py:205; canonical common/numeric.py:47. Related not duplicate: #5524. Extends prior path step 4.
findings.verifier_reproduction: `grep -rnE 'Decimal\(str\((round\()?float' lambdas mcp` returns 13 sites. `grep -rnE 'def _(to_)?dec'` finds 13 private helpers, including milestone_ledger.py:409 _dec, daily_metrics_compute_lambda.py:525 and daily_insight_compute_lambda.py:1929 and episode_detect_lambda.py:71 _to_dec (each `Decimal(str(round(float(val), 4)))`), coach_baseline.py:205 _dec (same body), and circadian_compliance_lambda.py:80. The canonical function is common/numeric.py:47 floats_to_decimal, which maps NaN/Inf to None and has precision=None by default. tests/test_numeric.py:77 says the #1207 precision parameter 'subsumes the round(4)/round(6) local variants', yet those local variants are still there. The divergence matters: the local `_to_dec(float('nan'))` gives Decimal('NaN'), and boto3 TypeSerializer then raises 'Infinity and NaN not supported'. The canonical helper writes None.
findings.already_fixed_or_filed: Adjacent to two items: #5524 item (c), which asks for an AST Decimal gate and deletion of the HAE floats_to_decimal copy but does not list these _to_dec/_dec copies, and the #5928 row 'principal path-to-A 4', which folds milestone_ledger._dec into numeric. This finding adds the other ~12 local helpers and the NaN divergence; attach it to one of those rather than filing a new issue.

findings.summary: Gate census blind spot: 92 source files walk `X = ...` but not `X: T = ...` while 680 module constants are annotated.
findings.evidence: scripts/gate_census.py 'AnnAssign exposure' n=92 files, 680 constants. Adjacent to #5524; not shown to be the same walkers.
findings.verifier_reproduction: `python3 scripts/gate_census.py` prints its own 'AnnAssign exposure (taxonomy instance 5, measured)' section: 92 source files and 680 annotated module constants. The measure is a syntactic proxy (gate_census.py:1081-1089, 1229-1252): a file that matches `ast.Assign` and not `ast.AnnAssign`. Spot checks show real latent blindness. deploy/sync_doc_metadata.py:373 finds CYCLE_GENESES only through ast.Assign, and deploy/endpoint_registry.py:82 finds ROUTES the same way, so annotating either constant would make the walker return None or empty without any error. Today both are unannotated (site_api_data.py:108 `CYCLE_GENESES = {`, site_api_lambda.py:380 `ROUTES = {`), so no current miss has been shown. The census's line 'Every constant in the second set is invisible to every walker in the first' overstates the problem: most of the 92 walkers never look at most of the 680 constants.
findings.already_fixed_or_filed: No open issue specific to it. The closed #2789 fixed one instance. Adjacent to #5524 (guards that cannot see new shapes).
findings.corrected_cause: This is a latent hazard per walker, not a live blind spot. The census already measures and reports it on every run (seeded 2026-08-13). No walker is shown missing a constant that exists today.

findings.summary: Chronicle syndication dates are the week-end dateline, not the publication date
findings.evidence: RSS /feed.xml item 'The Rate Flag' pubDate Tue 10 Nov 12:00; posts.json date 2026-11-10; the permalink JSON-LD datePublished and /story/ both say 13 Nov. Same offset for the 6 Oct item (site says 9 Oct) and the 13 Oct item (site says 17 Oct). A feed reader shows an item dated 3 days before it existed.
findings.regression_guard: Contract test that RSS pubDate equals the manifest's published_at, not the dateline.
findings.verifier_reproduction: curl https://averagejoematt.com/feed.xml (200, 6968 bytes, 9 items): 'The Rate Flag' pubDate 'Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:00:00 +0000'; 'The Quiet Accumulation' 13 Oct; 'Park's Blind Spot' 06 Oct. The live chapter pages say otherwise: /story/week-12/ header reads 'published 13 November 2026' and its JSON-LD has datePublished "2026-11-13"; /story/week-09/ says 'published 17 October 2026'; /story/week-08/ says 'published 9 October 2026'. /journal/posts.json has date 2026-11-10, 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-06 for those posts. scripts/v4_build_rss.py:140 writes the pubDate as rfc822(p['date']).

findings.verifier_reproduction: curl /subscribe/ (200): the meta description, og:description, the lede and the 'what you get' row all say 'the weekly write-up every Wednesday' / 'the Chronicle installment on Wednesday'. findings.verifier_reproduction: Ran live axe with the vendored tests/vendor/axe.min.js through qa/a11y_audit.run_axe, using Playwright Chromium with service workers blocked. Covered light and dark, at 1280x900 and 390x844, after scroll-reveal. Pages: /data/, /data/habits/, /data/training/, /data/vitals/, /coaching/ (20 page-renders). Live build dbf31ad. findings.summary: The drift sentinel's S3 lifecycle check cannot clear. It compares the declared ISO string with the boto3 datetime, so the forensic-retention rule reads as drift forever, and the remediation agent has handed it off verbatim on every run since 11-09 with a wrong fix ('expiration date slipped ... cdk deploy').
findings.evidence: deploy/drift_sentinel.py:527-530 `_lifecycle_rule_diff` uses `expected_rule.get(k) != live_rule.get(k)`. deploy/s3_lifecycle.json:103 has "Date": "2027-05-03T00:00:00Z". get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration returns 2027-05-03T00:00:00+00:00 (the same instant). Running `drift_sentinel.check_s3_lifecycle()` locally → {'status':'drift','changed_rule_ids':['forensic-journal-privacy-expire-2027-05-03'],'expected_count':16,'live_count':16}. The rule was added on 2026-11-05 (dad30b13c), and the drift line appears in the remediation logs of 11-09, 11-11 and 11-13.
findings.regression_guard: A contract test that round-trips every s3_lifecycle.json rule through a boto3-shaped (datetime) live rule and asserts no diff.
findings.verifier_reproduction: Graded tree a24ea2796. deploy/drift_sentinel.py:527-530 `_lifecycle_rule_diff` compares raw dicts with `!=`. deploy/s3_lifecycle.json:103 declares "Date": "2027-05-03T00:00:00Z". `aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration` returns 16 rules; the forensic rule's Expiration Date is the same instant. boto3 parses it to a datetime, so a str-vs-datetime compare can never be equal. I ran `drift_sentinel.check_s3_lifecycle()` read-only and got {'status':'drift','missing_rule_ids':[],'extra_rule_ids':[],'changed_rule_ids':['forensic-journal-privacy-expire-2027-05-03'],'expected_count':16,'live_count':16}. I pulled four remediation logs from s3://matthew-life-platform/remediation-log/2026/11/ (09/174433, 10/030811, 11/174410, 13/174317). Every one carries signals.drift.flagging.s3_lifecycle.changed_rule_ids=[forensic-journal-privacy-expire-2027-05-03] plus a needs_human line about it. The proposed fix changes from run to run, so 'verbatim' is wrong. 11-09: 'decide: update the repo rule to match live, or sync live to repo'. 11-10: 'cdk deploy LifePlatform*'. 11-11: 'Check cdk/stacks/storage_stack.py ... Run cdk deploy'. 11-13: 'Likely: expiration date slipped ... cdk deploy LifePlatformBackup'. All of these are wrong: lifecycle is owned by deploy/apply_s3_lifecycle.sh, not CDK. findings.summary: The HEAD-coverage zero-run discriminator puts 'web-flow' in BOT_COMMITTERS and checks it before anything else. Every squash merge to main is committed by web-flow, so a squash merge whose CI was swallowed (#2826 class) is labelled the non-failure 'bot-push-no-dispatch' and can never read 'swallowed'.
findings.evidence: scripts/check_main_green.py:385 `BOT_COMMITTERS = {"github-actions[bot]", "web-flow"}`. Lines 449-453 return ZR_BOT_PUSH_NO_DISPATCH before the `if not all_runs_at_head` swallow branch at :454, and ZR_NOT_A_FAILURE includes it (:391). Reproduced: classify_zero_run_head([], ['lambdas/web/site_api_lambda.py'], ['lambdas/**'], committer_login='web-flow') returns bot-push-no-dispatch; committer_login=None returns swallowed. The premise is false: `gh api commits/a24ea2796 --jq .committer.login` gives web-flow, and that sha has 10 workflow runs. `git log -500 --format=%cn origin/main` gives 407 GitHub (web-flow), 67 github-actions[bot], 26 integration. Added by aa3d3787b (#2927, 2026-08-20).
findings.regression_guard: Unit test: a web-flow committer with zero runs and in-scope paths must return swallowed; only github-actions[bot] (or a run-less reconcile marker) returns bot-push-no-dispatch.
findings.verifier_reproduction: Checked at a24ea2796. scripts/check_main_green.py:385 reads `BOT_COMMITTERS = {"github-actions[bot]", "web-flow"}`. In classify_zero_run_head, the committer test at :449-453 runs before the `if not all_runs_at_head` swallow branch. The caller (:915) takes commit.committer.login from `gh api commits/<sha>`. Run with sys.path=scripts: classify_zero_run_head([], ['lambdas/web/site_api_lambda.py'], ['lambdas/**'], committer_login='web-flow') returned {'state': 'bot-push-no-dispatch', ...}. The same call with committer_login=None returned {'state': 'swallowed', ...}. Live: `gh api repos/averagejoematt/life-platform/commits/a24ea2796 --jq .committer.login` returned web-flow (author averagejoematt), and actions/runs?head_sha gave total_count 10, so web-flow pushes do dispatch workflows. Over the last 500 commits on origin/main, `git log --format=%cn` counts 407 GitHub (web-flow), 67 github-actions[bot] and 26 integration. head_coverage_ok() counts ZR_BOT_PUSH_NO_DISPATCH in ZR_NOT_A_FAILURE, so a swallowed squash merge reads green. The intended suppression is the nightly reconcile push, and that comes from github-actions[bot] only. Searched issues for 'web-flow' and found nothing.
findings.already_fixed_or_filed: Not fixed: the newest commit touching the file, 544825e51, keeps the set. No matching issue found.
findings.corrected_cause: Root cause as stated. The fix is to drop 'web-flow' from BOT_COMMITTERS. Only a GITHUB_TOKEN push (github-actions[bot]) is suppressed from dispatching; web-flow commits dispatch normally.

findings.summary: The weekly recap share card shows a different weight than the home card and the pulse API on the same day
findings.evidence: moments/assets/week-2026-W46.png says '36.7 lbs down', 'as of 2026-11-14'. /api/pulse and home card OG say 38.8. Source is generated/public_stats.json (current_weight 290.65, stale vs 288.5), baked 12:30Z. og_moments.py:_sweep_week_recap reads stats.journey.
findings.extends: A.1 prior step 1 (sweep decoupled from the data writer)
findings.regression_guard: Test that the moments weight equals the pulse glyph scale value or the card is not emitted.
findings.verifier_reproduction: GET https://averagejoematt.com/moments/assets/week-2026-W46.png returns 200, a 1200x630 PNG, last-modified 2026-11-14 20:30:43 GMT. I viewed it: it reads '36.7 lbs down · HRV 58 ms · streak 0d · day 70' with the footer 'live numbers as of 2026-11-14'. GET /api/pulse (generated 2026-11-15T01:57Z) returns date 2026-11-14, glyphs.scale value 288.5, delta -38.8, delta_1d -2.2. A read-only `aws s3 cp s3://matthew-life-platform/generated/public_stats.json -` shows journey.current_weight_lbs 290.65 and lost_lbs 36.7, written by daily-brief-lambda at 18:01:22Z and refreshed at 2026-11-15T00:00Z, still 290.65. In the graded tree, lambdas/web/og_moments.py:300-319: _sweep_week_recap reads stats['journey'].lost_lbs and stamps the footer f"live numbers as of {datetime.now(PT):%Y-%m-%d}". On the same day the share card says 36.7 and pulse says 38.8.
findings.already_fixed_or_filed: Not filed. #5925 has share-card rows, but they cover missing per-page cards, not this disagreement. #5421 (og-image-generator timeout) does not cover it. git log on og_moments.py shows no fix for this.
findings.corrected_cause: The mechanism is right, with one sharpening. The card's 'as of' date is the render-time wall clock, not the date of the data it shows. It renders public_stats.journey, which holds the weigh-in before today's (290.65 vs 288.5: pulse's delta_1d of -2.2 puts yesterday at about 290.7). So the card states the previous weigh-in under today's date. I did not establish whether today's weigh-in existed when the daily brief wrote public_stats at 18:01Z. P1 looks high for a 2.1 lb gap on one share card; P2 fits better.

growth.coverage_statement: Graded the live site against main, with the live build slightly lagging main; I did not diff the two. I did not sample the Monday digest email or any SES send log (A.3 and A.4 UNOBSERVED). I did not assess the podcast feed (dark), Instagram or other social surfaces, or the Bluesky/X links. Subscriber list size read from DynamoDB (counts and timestamps only, no emails)."
